timeline.title: Pataliputra becomes a major ancient city
timeline.summary: Patna's documented history reaches back to Pataliputra and the Magadha world; the district history page places the city's historical beginning around the 6th century BCE.

timeline.title: Mauryan capital
timeline.summary: The Patna district history records Chandragupta Maurya making Pataliputra his capital in the 4th century BCE.

timeline.title: Patna's revival under Sher Shah Suri
timeline.summary: The district history describes a revival of Patna in the 16th century under Sher Shah Suri.

timeline.title: Patna as a trading centre
timeline.summary: Historical accounts cited in the Patna history record describe Patna as a major eastern trading centre and note the reputation of Patna rice in European markets.

timeline.title: Bihar cuisine as a seasonal, ingredient-led food culture
timeline.summary: Bihar Tourism describes a cuisine built around rice, seasonal produce, mustard oil, dairy and relatively simple preparations; the official material lists a broader North/East Indian culinary mixture.

timeline.title: Patna Kalam and everyday life
timeline.summary: The Patna district describes Patna Kalam as a painting tradition created by Mughal artists in the 18th century, with everyday life among its defining subjects. This is useful cultural context for the archive's visual storytelling, not a food claim.

timeline.title: A fragmented but active contemporary food map
timeline.summary: Recent community discussions repeatedly surface corridors such as Boring Road, Maurya Lok and Old Museum Road/Khao Gali alongside dish-specific stops. These are community signals and require field verification before being treated as canonical facts.
